findings.title: `unset --project` remediation contradicts the delete routing rule
findings.description:
Line 89 says delete "mirrors write", so deleting a personal key at project scope targets `.context-forge.local.toml`. The collision rule (line 146) and walkthrough step 9 (line 259) then tell the user to run `cf config unset git.integration_branch --project` to clear the stale copy in the shared file.

Under the stated routing, that command does the opposite of what the design intends:
- **Collision case:** it deletes the developer's personal value (the one the collision rule exists to protect) and leaves the stale shared copy, which then wins through the read fallback.
- **Walkthrough step 9:** the step cannot pass as written, because `cf check` will still report the finding.
- **Pre-migration case:** the key is only in the shared file, so `unset --project` is a silent no-op and the value keeps resolving.

The design needs to define delete semantics for a personal key that is present in the shared file. Two options that fit the existing shape:
- Delete removes the key from both project files.
- `migrate-personal` gains an explicit way to drop the stale shared copy.

findings.title: Gitignore coverage only reaches projects created after this slice
findings.description:
The ignore line is written only by `cf init`. Projects that already exist, which includes every project in the migration case, never get it.

In those projects, `cf config set git.integration_branch … --project` or `cf config migrate-personal` creates an un-ignored `.context-forge.local.toml`. The next `git add .` commits it. That leaves the plan's "must never be committed" requirement unmet, and the Overview's claim that `cf init` and `cf check` "keep personal settings out of git" does not hold there.

`cf check` has no finding for "personal file exists but is not ignored". The design should close this path with one of:
- Reuse the same ensure-ignored helper from `migrate-personal`.
- Add a `cf check` warning for an un-ignored personal file.

Separately, the "substring" check would treat `!.context-forge.local.toml` or a commented-out line as already covered. Specify a whole-line match on trimmed lines.

findings.title: No owner specified for raw per-file access needed by the checker and migrate command
findings.description:
The design fixes `ConfigManager`'s public API as unchanged and says callers never choose a file. Two new consumers need exactly what that API hides:
- The `ConsistencyChecker` rule must enumerate personal keys physically present in the shared file.
- `migrate-personal`, placed in the CLI's `config.ts`, must write to one specific file and delete from the other.

The design does not say where that logic lives. The design names the TOML helpers as living in `ConfigManager.ts` (line 93). As written, the implementer must either export those internals to the CLI and introspection, or duplicate file handling in two places. Both break the "routing lives inside `ConfigManager`" decision at lines 128-132.

Name a single core-level owner (for example, a find-misplaced operation and a migrate operation in the config module) that both the checker and the CLI call. The Component Structure listing should reflect it.

findings.title: Migration story omits the effect on teammates once the migration is committed
findings.description:
The plan requires a defined compat story for projects that already committed personal keys. The design covers the developer who runs the migration, but not the rest of the team.

`migrate-personal` edits the tracked `.context-forge.toml`. When that deletion is committed and pulled, every other developer's `git.integration_branch` falls through to user/default with no warning. The `cf check` finding has also disappeared for them, because the key is no longer in the shared file.

For this key, the fall-through changes the fork and merge target to `main`. That is the outcome the integration-branch setting exists to prevent. The Risk Assessment (line 264) says there is "no functional regression", which holds only for a single checkout.

State the intended team procedure (each developer migrates or sets their own value before the shared-file deletion lands) and surface it in the command's output or the finding text.

findings.title: Test requirements omit behaviours the design defines
findings.description:
The listed `migrate-personal` tests are "happy path + no-op path" only. The design specifies more behaviour that has no required test:
- **Collision branches:** skip when the personal value differs; delete the shared copy when the values are identical.
- **Per-key failure:** continue past a failed key and report `failed: <error>`.
- **`cf init` gitignore:** the create, append and already-present branches.

Without the failure-path test, the enumerated failure mode has no asserted observable signal. The exit status of `migrate-personal` when a key fails is also unspecified; define it as non-zero so the failure is not silent to scripts.

findings.title: Frontmatter dependency differs from the plan entry
findings.description: The frontmatter lists `dependencies: [914]`, while the plan entry says "Dependencies: none". 914 is complete, so this has no practical effect. Align one of the two for consistency.
